name: CoW Protocol solver SwapGuard unprotected call

classification.summary: A whitelisted solver's SwapGuard helper exposed an entry point that executed caller-supplied interactions with no access control, so the attacker routed a settlement through it and moved GPv2Settlement's DAI buffer to itself.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/cow.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.
One or more target block, transaction, ordering, or creator anchors remain unresolved.

sources.note: onchain review: SwapGuard 0xcD07a7695E3372aCD2B2077557DE93e667B92bd8 created 2023-01-25T15:43:35Z by 0x37ec2a900632cea128f4c9ebc3a2a95659c2c567, unrelated to the attack sender 0xc0e82c1e...; no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment (12.5 days). The tx receipt shows 114,824.89 DAI leaving GPv2Settlement 0x9008D19f58AAbD9eD0D60971565AA8510560ab41 for the attacker; the ~$166K headline figure covers the full set of assets taken. The settlement contract itself behaved as designed - the flaw is in the solver helper, so that is recorded as the victim contract.

limitations: Classification and loss came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/cow.json; legacy measurement.status=OK is provenance only.
